## Acceptance criteria

**AC1 — the predicate is executed, not matched.** The qualifying rule is published as a callable and CALLED in careerair-check.mjs against synthetic rows with a frozen clock. Asserting it by source regex is explicitly insufficient: this same file already recorded a mutant that survived a regex assertion.
**AC2 — boundaries hold.** Exactly 7 days, 7 days + 1 second, a future timestamp, null, empty string, whitespace, garbage, and each of the four statuses. A null firstSeen renders WITHOUT the lozenge. Note the trap you named: new Date(null) is 1 January 1970, not Invalid Date.
**AC3 — every new defence is mutation-tested.** Break each on purpose, show the check goes red, and assert a non-zero executed count. A check that can pass by doing nothing eventually will.
**AC4 — contrast passes in BOTH themes**, on measured figures rather than asserted ones, using the existing warning token rather than a new one.
**AC5 — 247 simultaneous lozenges do not make the page unreadable**, and the marker never overlaps the status control or steals width from the role title.
**AC6 — the browser-clock limitation is written where a future reader finds it** — beside the predicate and in the README.
# guidance: each independently checkable. If automatic, no AC may be satisfiable by a manual invocation of the delivered script alone.
